newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO end firm, investors wait for 6% 10-yr yield.
newsitem.headline: OLO end firm, investors wait for 6% 10-yr yield.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds ended higher on Thursday, slightly outperforming Bunds, as the market awaits direction from U.S. May jobs data on Friday US-ECI.
Dealers said trade was very thin and investors were virtually absent from the market.
"People are waiting to see six percent (on the benchmark 10-year bond). At yield levels below this they just do not buy any paper," one broker said.
The 2007 OLO BE286= closed with a yield of 5.89 percent, down from 5.91 percent on Wednesday, offering seven basis points over equivalent Bunds after Wednesday's eight MEUR.
Dealers said the Treasury's state note issuance programme was not doing well for the same reason -- investors prefer to park their cash in the bank rather than commit long-term at low rates.

The Treasury said on Wednesday that its latest issue of two notes reached a final 8.175 billion francs. Belgium hopes to raise 54 billion francs from four note issues planned for 1997/1998. Last year it raised 53 billion francs when it had targeted 80 billion.

One dealer noted the Treasury had taken more money than what was at expiry at recent T-bills auctions, while being stingy at recent OLO auctions. "Obviously, the Treasury believes that low short-term rates are here to stay," he said.
